learn.title: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval
learn.headline: Similar wrong facts hurt retrieval far more than long text does.
learn.reason: Shows why RAG fails: rival facts matter more than context length.

card.headline: In long inputs, look-alike facts confuse AI models, not length
card.gist: Researchers asked small open AI models to find one fact inside long text. Extra harmless text did not hurt them. Text that looked like the fact, or gave a rival answer, hurt a lot.
card.picture: Think of looking up one customer ID in a huge table. Millions of unrelated rows do not confuse you. Two rows with the same ID but different values do.
card.why_you: When you feed found documents into a model, near-duplicates and conflicting versions may matter more than total length. Cleaning them out could help more than shortening the text.
card.remember: Look-alike facts hurt more than long text does.
card.term_meaning: The drop in a model's accuracy when its input text gets longer.
card.say_it: In retrieval, context rot seems driven by competing look-alike facts, not raw length, so I remove conflicting chunks.
card.follow_up_why: Look-alikes pull the model's attention off the real evidence, and that lost attention tracked the failures.
card.reality_check: One research paper testing five small open models; the authors released their probe and measurements.
card.try_it: In Ollama, hide 'Key A = 7' inside filler text and ask for A. Then add 'Key A = 3' and ask again.
